Private VPC vs Hosted routing during failover
Perf benchmarking and canary rollout plan
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, will keep this to 45-ish minutes but happy to go longer. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dana: Dana here.
[00:10] Ethan: Ethan here.
[00:12] Lina: Lina on infra.
[00:15] Marcus (SE): Marcus from Redwood SE.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, CSM.
[00:20] Alex: Cool, agenda — capacity bump for Q4, adding a eu region, KMS and SSO checklist, and commercial amendment. Dana do you want to open with current usage?
[00:32] Dana: Yeah. So right now our prod is hitting about 1.9M tokens/day peak last week, average's lower but we want headroom. We had some unexpected campaign traffic and the AI features for search increased. We're forecasting 3.5M tokens/day for Nov-Dec.
[00:48] Ethan: To add, latency over the weekend spiked; some requests went to the Hosted tier and we saw 250-300ms p95 on short prompts which is above our 150ms target. We're trying to understand if that's routing or kv cache warm issues.
[01:05] Marcus: Ok thanks. A few quick things — p95 depends heavily on batching and KV cache hit-rate, plus model variant. Are you on the quantized runtime or full fp32?
[01:16] Lina: We're using the q4_8 profile for cost reasons, but might move to a higher perf profile for critical routes. Also we use prefix caching for common user prompts.
[01:28] Marcus: Right, so two levers — increase dedicated capacity to reduce queueing, and alter batching configs on low-latency routes. For the weekend spike, I suspect routing fallback to a lower tier model during saturation.
[01:42] Dana: That makes sense. On the committed side, we're open to a 20-30% bump in reserved capacity but want the amendment to include burst credits so we don't overcommit.
[01:52] Alex: Absolutely. We can add a burst pool and a conservative ramp schedule. We'll show a sample amendment that includes X burst token-equivalents per month.
[02:02] Ethan: Also we need to add eu-central-2. Our GDPR team insists EU-residency for certain workloads and low latency for EMEA customers.
[02:11] Priya: We do support eu-central-2; we can provision as a new geocluster and replicate model artifacts. There is a short lead time for cold-starts and model pull.
[02:20] Marcus: Technical note — if you want strict residency we recommend a staged migration: spin up eu-central with dedicated pool, deploy model variants, run canary traffic at 10-20% then cutover. KV cache priming helps.
[02:33] Lina: How long to prime cache? We have a 5M+ user prompt corpus, can't warm everything.
[02:40] Marcus: You don't need to warm everything. Targeted priming of top intents and using prefix/KV pre-warm jobs over the first 72 hours usually covers the 90% of common paths.
[02:53] Dana: On security — we're using their KMS for keys and need HSM-backed key protections. Do you do BYOK?
[02:59] Alex: Yes, Redwood supports BYOK via KMS integrations; we also have an on-prem HSM option for Private deployments. We'll share the KMS integration doc.
[03:09] Ethan: For SOC2, auditor asked for audit logs retention longer than 12 months. Is that configurable?
[03:14] Priya: We have an enterprise observability add-on that extends retention to 24 months and provides exportable audit logs. We'll include that in the packet.
[03:21] Lina: Network wise we want VPC peering to avoid egress. Is eu cluster able to peer to our EU VPC?
[03:27] Marcus: Yes, VPC peering for the eu cluster is supported; there is a network checklist — NAT, route tables, and a small firewall rule set. We'll share the template.
[03:36] Dana: Pricing — last year we did a 12-month commit. For this bump what are options — monthly add-ons or amend + prorated commit?
[03:43] Alex: Options: 1) Amendment to current contract adding X reserved units (pro-rated for remainder year) + burst credits; 2) Start a new 12-month commitment that begins at the next billing cycle. Most customers prefer amendment to avoid contract churn.
[03:55] Ethan: We want the amendment but need to see the SLA change — specifically p95 latency target for short prompts during peak must be <= 200ms.
[04:05] Alex: We can include a latency SLO for the dedicated pool with credits for violations. Note that p95 stacks in with network and app-level latency — we can add tracing tags so you can separate infra vs app.
[04:18] Marcus: On the perf side, I'll run a 24-hour throughput sweep on staging that mirrors your peak qps (you gave us the trace) and we'll provide token-level breakdowns, KV hit-rate, and tail latency. That should show whether routing is causing the 250ms spikes.
[04:34] Dana: Great. Can you also test with the q4_12 variant? We want to compare cost vs latency.
[04:40] Marcus: Yep — will include q4_8 and q4_12 comparisons and a quantized/fp32 note.
[04:46] Lina: For EU data residency, are logs stored in-region too? Our GDPR team requires audit and logs stay in EU.
[04:54] Priya: We can configure log export to your EU S3 or GCS bucket and retain copies only in-region per the compliance package.
[05:02] Ethan: Are there any lead times to get eu cluster active? We have a scheduled marketing push Nov 1.
[05:08] Marcus: Typical lead time for a new geocluster is 3–4 weeks for model pulling and smoke testing, add another week if you want private connect or an HSM provision. So timeline aligns but we should start provisioning late Sep.
[05:22] Dana: Ok, that matches our internal timeline.
[05:24] Alex: Commercially, I'll draft the amendment with the 25% reserved bump, include X number of burst credits, and a trial window for the EU cluster with no extra charge for first 30 days. Sound fair?
[05:35] Ethan: Sounds reasonable, assuming the SLA language is tight.
[05:38] Priya: We'll also attach the SOC2 + pen test summaries and the KMS playbook.
[05:44] Lina: One more infra ask — during canary, we want a fallback policy that route to US region if eu is saturated, but keep data residency flags on certain routes. Is that doable?
[05:55] Marcus: Yes, smart routing can be policy-encoded: route by latency or residency tag, and failover to US only for non-residency-protected routes. We'll map the routes you flag.
[06:07] Dana: Are there cost implications for that routing complexity?
[06:10] Alex: Minimal; primary costs are extra egress if you cross-regions, but with VPC peering and local model artifacts egress is low. We'll show estimates in the amendment.
[06:20] Ethan: Also curious about autoscaling — if the EU pool is dedicated, can we allow controlled burst into Redwood Hosted as overflow?
[06:28] Marcus: You can — we support an overflow policy that sends overflow to a lower-priority pool; billing is tracked separately and can be capped. That gives you headroom without overcommitting on reserved units.
[06:40] Dana: Good. For the perf sweep, what logs will you need? We can share traces and a representative prompt sample.
[06:46] Marcus: The request traces, average and peak qps profile, and a small set of golden prompts. Also your error patterns — 500s, timeouts.
[06:55] Ethan: We'll prepare that and drop into the shared folder.
[06:58] Priya: I'll create an invite for the security deep-dive next week with our security architect and your team.
[07:05] Alex: Cool. Any blockers on road to amendment sign?
[07:08] Dana: Just internal procurement — we need cost numbers and SLA language to present.
[07:12] Alex: We'll aim to have the amendment draft and pricing by Tue (09/14). Marcus will deliver perf sweep by Fri (09/17). Priya will send security package by 09/15.
[07:22] Ethan: Thanks. One note — we've been looking at CloudMega's new preempt pool pricing; can you comment on cost delta?
[07:29] Alex: CloudMega has aggressive spot pricing but typically higher variance and less predictable latency; Redwood focuses on predictable unit economics with our Dedicated + burst model. We'll include a competitive notes sheet.
[07:40] Dana: Ok good to have that.
[07:42] Marcus: Also we'll include a canary playbook with rollback criteria and runbook steps for priming KV cache.
[07:50] Lina: Perfect.
[07:52] Alex: Wrap up — I'll circulate the amendment, Marcus will run the sweep, Priya sends security docs, Ethan/Dana will confirm procurement timing. Next call after perf readout and security deep-dive to finalize sign.
[08:05] Dana: Thanks everyone.
[08:07] Ethan: Thanks.
[08:08] Alex: Appreciate it, bye.
[08:10] (recording ends)
